title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: M is a free Z/4-module of rank 2 (in the elliptic-curve application, E[4] in characteristic ≠ 2), and M_0 = M/2M ≅ F_2^2. J = M_0* is the 3-element set of nonzero vectors, Aut(M_0) ≅ S_J ≅ S_3, and ω = ω_{M_0} is the 2-element set of orientations of J, identified with the two 3-cycles ρ, ρ' = ρ^{-1}.

The previous page embeds two S_3-stable subspaces in End(M_0) = M_2(F_2):
(i) M_0 ↪ End(M_0), sending x_i to the transvection σ_i fixing x_i. Linearity holds because σ_1+σ_2+σ_3 = 0.
(ii) F_2^ω ↪ End(M_0), sending the two points of ω to ρ, ρ'. Since ρ^2+ρ+1 = 0, we get ρ+ρ' = id.

This page states three facts.
(15) The two subspaces are orthogonal for the trace form Tr(uv). Indeed σ_iρ is again a transposition, so it has trace 0.
(16) sl(M_0) = ker(tr) = M_0 ⊕ F_2·id. The σ_i have trace 0, and id has trace 2 = 0 in characteristic 2.
(17) F_2^ω ∩ sl(M_0) = F_2·id, since tr ρ = 1.
Together, End(M_0) = M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω as S_3-modules: a 2+2 dimensional split decomposition, even though char 2 divides |S_3|. Here F_2^ω is the permutation module on S_3/A_3, i.e. S_3 acts through the sign.

Consequence: the torsor P_M under V_J(M_0) ≅ End(M_0) splits canonically into a pair of torsors. On the previous page, P_M parametrises M as a twisted form, with M_i = P_M ∧ (M_0, pr_i). The pair is I_M, an M_0-torsor (an affine F_2-plane), and S_M, an F_2^ω-torsor.

Theorem: M ↦ (M_0, I_M, S_M) is an equivalence between the groupoid of free rank-2 Z/4-modules and the groupoid of triples (M_0 a rank-2 F_2-space, I an M_0-torsor, S an F_2^{ω(M_0)}-torsor).

Corollary: there is an isomorphism of exact sequences
1 → End(M_0) → GL(M) → GL(M_0) ≅ S_3 → 1
with
1 → M_0 × F_2^ω → Aut(M_0, I_M, S_M) → GL(M_0) → 1.
The kernel map is u ↦ id + 2ũ, for any lift ũ of u.

Marginal note: this is essentially GL(2, Z/4) ≅ GL(2, F_2) ⋉ M_2(F_2), with M_2(F_2) ≅ F_2^2 × F_2^ω as S_3-modules. In (19) the condition reads SL(2, Z/4) ≅ {g·u ∈ S_3·M_2(F_2) | sg(g)·e(Tr u) = 1}, where e: F_2 ≅ ±1. This follows from det(g(1+2u)) = det(g)(1+2 tr u) mod 4 and det(g) = sgn(g) for the S_3 lifted from GL_2(Z).

The next page converts the data combinatorially:
- (M_0, I) becomes a 4-element set I;
- (ω, S) becomes a combinatorial square Q with its two codiagonals C(Q);
- these are glued by k: ω(I) ≅ C(Q).
This yields GL_{Z/4}(M) ≅ S_I ×_{±1} D_Q (sign × codiagonal character). The order check works: 24·8/2 = 96 = |GL_2(Z/4)|.

Purpose: a canonical, coordinate-free combinatorial description of level-4 structures (E[4]) for the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: Formula (19) in the marginal note ends with '= ' with nothing written after it; it should read '= 1' (or 'e(Tr u) = sg(g)'). This is an omission, not a mathematical error.

The page does not state that the extension splits, but it does split: the finite S_3 ⊂ GL_2(Z) injects into GL_2(Z/4), since the level-4 congruence kernel is torsion-free. This justifies the semidirect product claimed in the marginal note.
Implicitly the direct sum End = M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω needs M_0 ∩ F_2^ω = 0. This holds (the span of the σ_i does not contain id), but it is not written out.

ideas.what: Canonical S_3-equivariant decomposition End_{F_2}(F_2^2) = M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω (transvections ⊕ span of the 3-cycles), orthogonal for the trace form, with sl_2 = M_0 ⊕ F_2·id
ideas.modern_name: decomposition of M_2(F_2) as a GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 module

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids: free rank-2 Z/4-modules ≃ triples (M_0, M_0-torsor, F_2^ω-torsor)
ideas.modern_name: classification of rank-2 Z/4-lattices via torsors of liftings (non-abelian H^1 / twisted forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution; this canonical form is not standard

ideas.modern_name: structure of GL_2(Z/4) as a split extension of GL_2(F_2) by the congruence kernel

ideas.what: (Next page) GL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{±1} D_4, realised combinatorially by a 4-set I, a square Q and an isomorphism of orientations with codiagonals
ideas.modern_name: fibre-product description of GL_2(Z/4); combinatorial level-4 structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; the isomorphism type is known in group tables, but this canonical groupoid form is not standard

missed.claim: A canonical (functorial, groupoid-level) equivalence between free rank-2 Z/4-modules and combinatorial triples (M_0, I, S), later (I, Q, k). This gives a coordinate-free 'combinatorial level-4 structure' model for E[4]. The isomorphism type of GL_2(Z/4) is known; the canonical torsor splitting and the groupoid equivalence appear not to be written down as such.
missed.quote: Le foncteur M ↦ (M_0, I_M, S_M) ... équivalence de groupoïdes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a canonical combinatorial description of level-4 structures on elliptic curves, e.g. for the moduli stack M(4) or dessins and Teichmüller-tower considerations. It is modest, essentially elementary group theory made canonical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct but elementary: a decomposition of M_2(F_2) as an S_3-module and the split structure of GL_2(Z/4). The only mildly distinctive feature is the canonical groupoid/torsor formulation, which feeds the combinatorial (I, Q, k) model of level-4 structures on the next page. It is a nice unpublished framing, not a surprising result.
transcription_corrections: In (19) the condition should read 'sg(g) e(Tr u) = 1'; the right-hand side is blank in the manuscript.
In the margin, 'Gl(2,Z/4Z) ≃ Gl(2,F_2)·[M_2(F_2)]' is better read as 'Gl(2,Z/4Z) ≃ Gl(2,F_2) ⋉ M_2(F_2) (produit semi-direct)'.
In (16) the struck-out symbol before sl(M_0) is a crossed-out 'M_0'-like scribble; the intended statement is sl(M_0) = ker(tr) = M_0 ⊕ F_2 id_{M_0}.
In the Theorem the source category is 'Z/4Z-modules libres de rang 2'.
